newsitem.title: USA: U.S Nov consumer credit rose $7.4 billion.
newsitem.headline: U.S Nov consumer credit rose $7.4 billion.

text.p: U.S. consumer credit grew $7.4 billion in November at a 7.4 percent annual rate after rising a revised $6.5 billion in October at a 6.7 percent annual rate, the Federal Reserve said Wednesday
Auto credit outstanding rose $500 million in November at a 1.5 percent annual rate after being up $1.0 billion in October at an annual rate of 3.1 percent.
Revolving or credit-card debt increased in November by $3.2 billion at a 8.5 percent annual rate, compared with an $1.4 billion October advance at a 3.8 percent annual rate.

Other credit, which includes consumer bank loans like those for mobile homes but not real estate mortgages, grew by $3.6 billion at a 12.3 percent annual rate in November after rising $4.1 billion at a 14.5 percent annual rate in October.
Before seasonal adjustment, total outstanding consumer credit in November was $1.20 trillion, up from $1.19 trillion in October and $1.10 trillion in November 1995.
The department had previously said total consumer credit rose by $2.2 billion in October.
